title: Adaptive learning selected an additive for a magnesium-air battery
summary: An iterative machine-learning adaptive-design workflow selected 2,3-dihydroxynaphthalene for a lab-made (Mg-0.2Ca)-air battery. The authors report a cell voltage of 1.82 V and 3.37 kWh kg⁻¹ specific energy calculated from total Mg-anode mass loss, not whole-cell or pack mass. The publisher abstract reports 83% anodic utilization, while the full article reports 85% at a stated 0.5 mA cm⁻² condition; this discrepancy is not resolved here and the utilization figure is omitted. The authors also state that the surrogate model overestimated performance predictions for this additive.
ai_technology: Iterative adaptive design with SOAP descriptors and a KPCovR surrogate model
organization: Institute of Surface Science, Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon; Hebei University of Technology; Kiel University

source_review.scope: Primary Elsevier indexed abstract and full publisher PDF text hosted by ResearchGate; primary Hereon repository metadata cross-check. Specific energy basis and internal utilization-efficiency discrepancy reviewed.

evidence.tested: The authors report a lab-made (Mg-0.2Ca)-air battery with the model-selected 2,3-dihydroxynaphthalene additive at 1.82 V. Reported specific energy is 3.37 kWh kg−1 calculated from total Mg-anode mass loss. No whole-cell or pack-mass specific energy is claimed.
evidence.unknown: Publisher abstract reports 83% anodic utilization; full article text gives 85% at a stated 0.5 mA cm−2 condition. The difference is unresolved, so no utilization percentage is asserted. The authors report that the surrogate model overestimated predictions for this additive.
evidence.ai_role: A SOAP-descriptor/KPCovR model in iterative adaptive experimental design contributed to selecting 2,3-dihydroxynaphthalene for electrochemical validation.
